[[EuroLeague]] | team = Real Madrid | number = 9 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2006|02|05|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Madrid]], Spain | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = 2022 | years1 = 2022–present | team1 = [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] | years2 = 2022–2024 | team2 = →[[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid B]] | highlights = | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{Flagu|Spain}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA U18 European Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2023 FIBA U18 European Championship|2023 Serbia]]|[[Spain men's national under-18 basketball team|Team]]}} | caption = González with Real Madrid in 2025 }} '''Hugo González Peña''' (born 5 February 2006) is a Spanish professional [[basketball]] player for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He also plays for the [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain national team]]. ==Early life and career== Born in [[Madrid]], both González' parents were professional basketball players, which made him start playing at age nine. He has said: "My first basketball memories come from my parents. They played basketball and they influenced me a bit.".{{Cite web |date=2025-05-28 |title=Next Big Thing: Hugo Gonzalez leading Spain's next generation |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/next-big-thing-hugo-gonzalez-leading-spains-next-generation |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}} He began playing for a local basketball academy in [[San Agustín del Guadalix]], where he stayed three years. González joined [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]]'s youth team at 9 years of age. He quickly rose through the ranks, eventually becoming a part of the junior team and the reserve team in the [[Liga EBA]] during the 2022–23 season. González became a star on the 2006 generation roster, which included Ismaila Diagne, Mitar Bonjakovic and fellow draft prospect [[Egor Demin]]. In 2023, he won the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Next Generation Tournament]] with Real Madrid U18. He won a back-to-back title in 2024, also gathering MVP honours. González scored 23 points and 6 assists in the championship game against PFBB, and averaged 17.5 points, 6.5 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game over the tournament.{{Cite web |date=2024-05-26 |title=Gonzalez crowned MVP after helping Real to repeat title {{!}} Adidas Next Generation Tournament |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/ngt/news/gonzalez-crowned-mvp-after-helping-real-to-repeat-title/ |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}} == Professional career == On October 2, 2022, González made his professional debut with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in the [[Liga ACB]] against [[Monbus Obradoiro]].{{Cite web |title=Hugo González debuts with Real Madrid |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/es-ES/es-ES/noticias |access-date=2023-12-02 |website=Real Madrid CF {{!}} Web Oficial del Real Madrid CF |language=es}} He spent 3:08 minutes on the court, contributing with 4 points and a [[Performance Index Rating|PIR]] of 5 in the win against the Galicians. At 16 years, 7 months, and 27 days old, he became the fourth youngest Madridista to play in the ACB.{{Cite web |date=2022-10-03 |title=Hugo González, el último niño prodigio del Real Madrid: debuta con 16 años y sigue la senda de Doncic y Garuba |url=https://www.marca.com/baloncesto/acb/2022/10/03/633a641246163ffe608b4581.html |access-date=2023-12-02 |website=MARCA |language=es}} == National team career == === Junior teams === In July 2022, González was part of the [[2022 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]] held in Málaga, where the team secured a silver medal by losing the final to the United States with a score of 67–79. On July 30, 2023, he won silver medal in the [[2023 FIBA U18 European Championship]] held in [[Niš]], Serbia, losing the final to the host team.{{Cite web |title=Topic, Bosnjakovic outduel Mara and Co as Serbia dethrone Spain |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2023/news/hosts-serbia-down-back-to-back-champs-spain-celebrate-return-to-top-of-podium |access-date=2023-12-02 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} === Senior team === In February 2025, González made his debut with the [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain national senior team]] when he had eleven points and six rebounds in a win over [[Latvia men's national basketball team|Latvia]] in the [[EuroBasket 2025 qualification]] round. ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===EuroLeague=== {{Euroleague player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 EuroLeague|2023–24]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] | 6 || 1 || 4.3 || .200 || .000 || 1.000 || .2 || .3 || {{sort|-|—}} || {{sort|-|—}} || 0.7 || -0.3 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"|Career | 6 || 1 || 4.3 || .200 || .000 || 1.000 || .2 || .3 || {{sort|-|—}} || {{sort|-|—}} || 0.7 || -0.3 {{S-end}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == * [https://www.acb.com/jugador/temporada-a-temporada/id/20213252 Hugo González] at [[Liga ACB|liga acb]] (in Spanish) * [https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/players/hugo-gonzalez/011649/ Hugo González] at [[EuroLeague|Euroleague]] {{Real Madrid Baloncesto current roster}} {{Euroleague NGT MVP}} {{DEFAULTSORT:González, Hugo}} [[Category:2006 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century Spanish sportsmen]] [[Category:Basketball players from Madrid]] [[Category:Liga ACB players]] [[Category:Real Madrid Baloncesto players]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Spanish men's basketball players]]
